Annular atrophic lichen planus | 99.73% | L5 | Research Question | Moderate — mechanism plausible, but high-potency steroids may paradoxically worsen existing skin atrophy
Lichen planus pemphigoides | 99.64% | L5→L4 (class) | Research Question | High — corticosteroids (topical and systemic) are established therapy for both LP and bullous pemphigoid components
Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma | 99.42% | L5 | **Hold** | Low — standard care is radiotherapy or rituximab; topical corticosteroids have no primary therapeutic role
Dermatitis | 99.30% | L5→L1 (class) | **Proceed with Guardrails** | Very High — direct mechanistic alignment; class-level Phase 3 RCT support from clobetasol and betamethasone
2-HEMA sensitization | 99.00% | L5 | **Hold** | Low — sensitization ≠ dermatitis; core intervention is allergen avoidance, not immunosuppression

Paraneoplastic Cerebellar Degeneration | 97.99% | L4 | Research Question
Intracerebral Hemorrhage | 99.79% | **L2** | **Proceed with Guardrails** | TRIDENT Phase 3 completed (n=1,671); NCT07458880 recruiting (n=140)
Cerebral Artery Occlusion | 99.89% | L3 | Research Question | 5 animal studies; 5 indirect clinical trials
MRI Defined Brain Infarct | 99.86% | L4 | Research Question | STEP trial (n=8,000; intensive BP control)
Malignant Renovascular Hypertension | 99.90% | L4 | Research Question | 2 paediatric case reports; strong mechanistic rationale
Pulmonary Hypertension (Lung Disease/Hypoxia) | 99.91% | L5 | **Hold** | Non-specific literature; known safety concern (see Safety section)
Polyclonal Hyperviscosity Syndrome | 99.63% | L5 | Hold | No mechanistic link; likely topological false positive from blood/infection node clustering in knowledge graph
Hyperamylasemia | 99.63% | L5 | Hold | Laboratory marker, not a treatment target; Amoxicillin can paradoxically *cause* drug-induced pancreatitis
Congenital Analbuminemia | 99.59% | L5 | Hold | Monogenic disease (*ALB* loss-of-function); no biological rationale for antibiotic intervention

Blood Group Incompatibility | 99.40% | L5 | Hold | Sole literature finding (PMID 40350274) is a coincidental *Campylobacter* bacteraemia in an ABO-mismatched HSCT patient — Amoxicillin treated an infection, not the incompatibility
Premalignant Haematological System Disease | 99.29% | L5 | Hold | MDS/CHIP/SMM require targeted or watch-and-wait strategies; no antibiotic mechanism relevant
Haematological Disease with Acquired Peripheral Neuropathy | 99.14% | L5 | Hold | Paraprotein/amyloid-driven neuropathies (POEMS, AL) require targeted blood disorder therapy; no antibiotic mechanism

Septicemic Plague | 99.13% | L4 | Research Question | *In vitro* and murine studies show β-lactam activity against *Y. pestis*; however, clinical guidelines recommend aminoglycosides or fluoroquinolones as first-line due to β-lactamase resistance concerns and intracellular penetration limitations

Macrothrombocytopenia with mitral valve insufficiency | 99.995% | L4 | Research Question | TPO-RA may raise platelet count; cannot correct structural defect. Class-effect from eltrombopag in MYH9-related disease.

Hereditary thrombocytopenia with normal platelets | 99.995% | L4 | Research Question | Normal platelet size excludes MYH9; transcription factor mutation subtypes (RUNX1, ANKRD26, ETV6) may respond to TPO-RA. Eltrombopag positive in ANKRD26-related cases.

Transient neonatal thrombocytopenia | 99.995% | L4 | Research Question | Mechanistically plausible (TPO-RA as rescue therapy in NAIT). Major safety concern: no pharmacokinetic/safety data in neonates for avatrombopag.
Dense granule disease | 99.995% | L5 | Hold | Storage pool defect (ADP/serotonin deficiency); platelet count usually normal. TPO-RA addresses quantity, not granule function. Likely false positive.
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis | 99.993% | L5 | Hold | Motor neuron degeneration (TDP-43/FUS/SOD1); no connection to TPO/c-Mpl pathway. Cluster pattern suggests systematic KG bias.
Bilateral parasagittal parieto-occipital polymicrogyria | 99.992% | L5 | Hold | Rare cortical malformation (TUBB2B, LAMC3 mutations); platelet counts typically normal. KG noise output.
Lower motor neuron syndrome with late-adult onset | 99.992% | L5 | Hold | ALS-spectrum anterior horn cell degeneration; no relation to platelet synthesis pathway.
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, susceptibility to | 99.991% | L5 | Hold | Redundant with rank 5 ALS entry; same mechanistic mismatch.
Mills syndrome | 99.991% | L5 | Hold | ALS variant (corticospinal tract); part of the same neurodegeneration cluster.
Monomelic amyotrophy | 99.990% | L5 | Hold | Hirayama disease (cervical anterior horn); benign, self-limiting. No TPO pathway relevance.
Primary Release Disorder of Platelets | 99.96% | Very Weak — genetic/intrinsic platelet defect, not immune-mediated | Hold
Pseudo-von Willebrand Disease | 99.96% | Very Weak — GPIbα gain-of-function mutation, genetic basis | Hold
Glanzmann Thrombasthenia | 99.88% | Very Weak — GPIIb/IIIa gene mutation, single-gene disorder | Hold
Severe Nonproliferative Diabetic Retinopathy | 99.05% | Weak — microvascular/metabolic disease; BAFF-B cell axis not established | Hold
Autosomal Dominant Macrothrombocytopenia | 99.04% | Very Weak — inherited megakaryocyte differentiation defect | Hold

Infectious Otitis Media | 99.30% | L4 | Hold | Narrow mechanistic link; cefoxitin covers few typical pathogens; MRSA/NTM angle only
Urinary Tract Infection | 99.26% | L3 | Research Question | 2 terminated Phase 4 RCTs + animal model support; ESBL-UTI niche is biologically plausible
Chronic Otitis Media | 99.12% | L4 | Research Question | Anaerobic coverage relevant; no direct cefoxitin-specific clinical data
Suppurative Otitis Media | 99.11% | L4 | Research Question | Cefoxitin acts as MRSA surrogate test marker — diagnostic role, not therapeutic
Middle Ear Disease | 99.11% | L3 | Hold | One 1982 unregistered case series for cholesteatoma surgery prophylaxis; insufficient evidence
Gonococcal Urethritis | 99.09% | L2 | **Proceed with Guardrails** | Strongest evidence; multiple 1979–1986 controlled trials; contemporary susceptibility data needed
Ureaplasma Urethritis | 99.09% | L5 | Hold | Biological contradiction — β-lactams have no activity against cell wall-deficient *Ureaplasma*
Toxocariasis | 99.09% | L5 | Hold | Biological contradiction — cefoxitin is an antibacterial; no antiparasitic activity against nematodes
Otosalpingitis | 99.08% | L5 | Hold | No evidence; theoretical partial coverage only
Non-Suppurative Otitis Media | 99.07% | L5 | Hold | Primarily non-bacterial (eustachian tube dysfunction, allergy, viral); antibiotics not indicated per guidelines
Ureaplasma urethritis | 99.89% | L5 | **Biologically implausible** — Ureaplasma lacks cell wall (no PBP target for beta-lactams)
Gonococcal urethritis | 99.89% | L5 | **Theoretically possible** but no MIC data or clinical trials; not in CDC/WHO STI guidelines
Uterine inflammatory disease | 99.88% | L5 | **Incomplete coverage** — PID requires anaerobic cover; ceftolozane alone is insufficient
Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis | 99.88% | L4 | **Indirect support only** — ceftolozane/tazobactam approved for cUTI; XGP usually requires surgery
Polyclonal hyperviscosity syndrome | 99.52% | L5 | **Biologically implausible** — immunoglobulin disorder unrelated to antibacterial mechanism
Hyperamylasemia | 99.52% | L5 | **Biologically implausible** — metabolic marker; beta-lactams may cause this as a side effect, not treat it
Urogenital tuberculosis | 99.50% | L5 | **Biologically implausible** — MTB expresses BlaC beta-lactamase; ceftolozane not active against MTB
Congenital analbuminemia | 99.44% | L5 | **Biologically implausible** — genetic albumin synthesis disorder; graph artifact via protein-binding nodes
Blood group incompatibility | 99.22% | L5 | **Biologically implausible** — ABO/Rh immune reaction; no antibacterial relevance
Premalignant hematological disease | 99.11% | L5 | **Biologically implausible** — clonal stem cell disorder; ceftolozane has no antiproliferative mechanism

Polyclonal Hyperviscosity Syndrome | 99.87% | L5 | Hold | No mechanistic basis; plasma viscosity is not reduced by antibiotics
Congenital Analbuminemia | 99.85% | L5 | Hold | Genetic (ALB gene) disease; antibiotics cannot correct albumin synthesis defects
Blood Group Incompatibility | 99.78% | L5 | Hold | Immunohematology problem; no biological relevance to antimicrobial therapy
Premalignant Hematological Disease | 99.73% | L5 | Hold | MDS/MGUS are clonal marrow disorders, not infection-driven

Monoclonal Gammopathy | 99.71% | L4 | Research Question | Evidence reflects prophylactic infection prevention in MM/HSCT patients — not disease-modifying for gammopathy itself
Hematological Disease + Peripheral Neuropathy | 99.68% | L5 | Hold | ⚠️ Safety contraindication: fluoroquinolones can induce or worsen peripheral neuropathy (FDA Black Box Warning 2016)
Ureaplasma urethritis | 99.93% | L4 | 4 papers (indirect) | **False positive** — cell wall-deficient organism; intrinsically resistant to all beta-lactams

Uterine inflammatory disease | 99.92% | L3 | 7 papers + 1 guideline | Mechanistically sound; French 2019 guideline supports use
Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis | 99.90% | L4 | 2 case reports | Surgery is primary treatment; antibiotic role is adjunctive only
Urogenital tuberculosis | 99.89% | L5 | 1 case report (unrelated) | **False positive** — TB requires RIPE regimen; meropenem (not amoxicillin) needed for MDR-TB
Abdominal cystic lymphangioma | 99.80% | L5 | None | **False positive** — congenital lymphatic malformation; no infectious etiology
Celiac trunk compression syndrome | 99.80% | L5 | None | **False positive** — vascular mechanical disease; no infectious etiology
Abdominal ectopic pregnancy | 99.80% | L5 | 1 unrelated trial | **False positive** — surgical/methotrexate treatment; retrieved trial studies hysteroscopy technique

Disease of uterine broad ligament | 99.79% | L5 | None | Partial mechanistic rationale for infectious cases only; zero supporting evidence
